notes:
Fake-backend package for Copy-v0, served by the Gymnasium family driver with native gym.envs.algorithmic:CopyEnv and a package fake. The upstream clone was never imported, installed or run, and the sim backend (gym.make('Copy-v0')) was not run; there is no hardware backend and no hardware run. The fake is a pure-Python re-implementation of CopyEnv and AlgorithmicEnv and was not compared with the upstream environment: it draws tapes and reset lengths with Python's random.Random while upstream uses numpy's RandomState, so one seed gives different tapes on the two. autoreset is enabled so a step after the environment's own short time limit starts the next episode instead of being refused; the output still reports terminated/truncated for the last tick. NOT COVERED: the Gymnasium bridge derives the Tuple action space as a length-3 items array without per-element bounds, so the runtime cannot enforce the movement (0..1), write flag (0..1) or character (0..4) elements; the fake checks them element by element exactly as algorithmic_env.py:163 asserts, and an invalid element is a device fault rather than an envelope refusal. This is also listed in the fidelity gaps and facts.md. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed is used by the next reset, so the seed call makes no native call) and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the integer inputs ticks, reset seed and seed that the bridge derives; no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. No extension capability ids were used, so there are no catalogue requests.
